newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end higher in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end higher in active trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended higher in active trade that saw gainers led by banks Bancoquia and Banco de Bogota and brewing giant Bavaria.

Medellin's IBOMED .IBMG general price index added 0.32 percent to close at 17,398.23 on trading volume of 2.7 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB .IBB closed up 1.17 percent, meanwhile, ending at 1,148.42 on a volume of nearly 2.8 billion pesos.
Blue-chip Bavaria, flagship of the Julio Mario Santo Domingo conglomerate, was among the most actively traded shares in Bogota.
The stock, which staged an impressive rally earlier this year, added another 1.25 percent in Bogota trade, closing at 8,000 pesos per share.
"It's been said that Bavaria's first quarter results were particularly good and that's being reflected in the share price," one Bogota-based trader said.

Cement maker Compania de Cemento Argos was also heavily traded in Bogota and closed up 0.41 percent, despite having reported Tuesday that its Q1 net profit fell 45 percent compared to the same period last year. The drop was largely due to extraordinary gains in the first quarter of last year.

The day's biggest winner by far was Bancoquia, however, which closed up 5.0 percent in Medellin at 3,150 pesos per share on market talk about it being on the verge of completing a merger agreement with Spain's Banco Santander.
Another gainer in bank stocks was Banco de Bogota, which closed up 1.8 percent in Medellin at 6,500 pesos per share.

Despite the day's gains, Bogota stock exchange president Carlos Caballero said he saw share prices holding mostly stable pending a possible cut in domestic interest rates. He also called some recent earnings reports "worrisome with respect to future share price action."
